study_identification_part.si_4_title: Multivariate brain-cognition associations in euthymic bipolar disorder

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Four public datasets (HCP-YA: n=1113, OpenBHB: n=3984, OASIS-3: n=542, Cam-CAN: n=644) were used to develop normative models of cortical thickness, along with a local Newcastle University cohort (NCL: n=61). The BLISS study recruited BD patients (n=56) and matched healthy controls (n=26) for clinical research. SINGLE-SITE refers to both the NCL cohort and the BLISS study cohort.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: We utilised four public datasets of T1-weighted scans from healthy controls: the WU-Minn Human Connectome Project Young Adult (HCP...); Open Big Healthy Brains (OpenBHB...); Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS-3...); and the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN...). We also used a cohort of healthy adult participants scanned at Newcastle University as part of another study (site=NCL).

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The four public datasets and NCL cohort were combined (total N=6344, after outlier removal N=5977) to build normative models of cortical thickness. BLISS healthy controls (n=26) were included in the normative model for site correction. BLISS BD patients (n=56) were the target for clinical brain-cognition association analysis using canonical correlation analysis (CCA).
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: To mitigate issues with a small healthy control sample, we developed normative models of cortical thickness using large public normative datasets... A sample of n=6344 healthy individuals were included... We harmonised the normative-HC data, including the 26 HCs recruited to BLISS, for each ROI... BD data were then adjusted for age, sex and scanning site, using the prediction from the normative model, where the site correction was informed by the site offset estimated for BLISS HCs.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The normative model was developed using N=6344 healthy individuals from five sources (HCP-YA: 1113, OpenBHB: 3984, OASIS-3: 542, Cam-CAN: 644, NCL: 61). After removing outliers (n=393, defined as residuals greater than 5 median absolute deviations in any ROI), the final sample was N=5951 (6344-393). However, the paper reports N=5977 in Figure 3 caption and supplementary Table S3. The study does not explicitly separate train/test phases for the normative model.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: A sample of n=6344 healthy individuals were included... We removed controls who had outliers in any ROI, defined as residuals greater than 5 median absolute deviations (n=393)... Abnormality scores were calculated for each region using normative modelling with a large normative reference sample (n=5977).
